title: Geometric Kernel Diversity: An Axiomatic Diversity Measure in Euclidean Space
abstract: arXiv:2610.19570v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Quantifying the diversity of a set of objects is a fundamental problem in machine learning and statistics. Mironov and Prokhorenkova (2025) recently showed that three axioms-monotonicity, uniqueness, and continuity-are crucial for a reliable diversity measure and that none of the standard metrics in the literature satisfy all three. They also constructed two measures that do satisfy the axioms, but both are NP-hard to compute, leaving open the question of whether efficient axiomatic diversity measures can exist. We study a Euclidean-restricted version of this question. We introduce Geometric Kernel Diversity (GKD), which associates a radial kernel solid with each point and measures the volume of their union. We show that canonical GKD satisfies all three Mironov-Prokhorenkova axioms on Euclidean-realizable inputs. For canonical GKD, we give exact polynomial-time algorithms in dimensions $d \le 3$. translated_title: 几何核多样性：欧几里得空间中的公理化多样性度量
translated_abstract: 量化一组对象的多样性是机器学习与统计学中的一个基本问题。Mironov 和 Prokhorenkova（2025）最近证明，三条公理——单调性、唯一性和连续性——对于可靠的多样性度量至关重要，而文献中的标准度量无一能同时满足这三条公理。他们还构造了两个满足这些公理的度量，但计算它们都是 NP 难的，这就留下了一个悬而未决的问题：是否存在高效的公理化多样性度量。我们研究了该问题在欧几里得空间受限情形下的版本。我们提出了几何核多样性，它为每个点关联一个径向核立体，并以这些立体的并集体积来度量多样性。我们证明，标准 GKD 在欧几里得可实现的输入上满足全部三条 Mironov-Prokhorenkova 公理。对于标准 GKD，我们在维度 d ≤ 3 时给出了精确的多项式时间算法；在任意维度下，我们给出了一个随机……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出几何核多样性（GKD）——通过为每个点关联径向核立体并度量其并集体积来衡量多样性——该度量在欧几里得空间中同时满足单调性、唯一性与连续性三条公理，且在维度 d ≤ 3 时可被精确的多项式时间算法求解，从而回答了此前关于高效公理化多样性度量是否存在的悬而未决的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Geometric Kernel Diversity (GKD), which measures diversity as the union volume of radial kernel solids associated with each point; GKD satisfies all three Mironov-Prokhorenkova axioms (monotonicity, uniqueness, continuity) on Euclidean-realizable inputs and admits exact polynomial-time algorithms in dimensions d ≤ 3, addressing the open question of whether efficient axiomatic diversity measures can exist.
